sections.title: What are Large Language Models?
sections.body: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are advanced computer systems that understand and generate human language. They are built using a type of artificial intelligence called neural networks, which learn from vast amounts of text data. This training helps them predict what words come next in a sentence.

sections.title: How Do LLMs Process Text?
sections.body: LLMs break down text into smaller pieces called tokens, which can be words, subwords, or even characters. These tokens are transformed into numerical representations, known as embeddings, that capture the meaning and relationships between words. This process allows LLMs to understand context and generate relevant responses.

sections.title: The Importance of Prompts
sections.body: Prompts are the questions or instructions we give to LLMs to guide their responses. Even small changes in a prompt can lead to very different outputs, making prompt design crucial for getting accurate answers. By carefully crafting prompts, we can improve the quality and relevance of the LLM's responses.

sections.title: Enhancing LLM Performance
sections.body: Techniques like prompt engineering and Chain-of-Thought prompting help refine how LLMs respond. Prompt engineering involves giving specific instructions to control the style and content of the output. Chain-of-Thought prompting encourages the model to show its reasoning step-by-step, which can lead to better answers, especially for complex tasks.
